Surface semivowel, the non-syllabic counterpart of the vowel i: stress placement suggests that vowels and semivowels are complementary (p. 661), and the diachronic paper says the semivowels are in complementary distribution with the corresponding vowels i, u (2022b: 684). It stands next to a vowel: after one (é.i̯u 'seven'), also as the offglide of the diphthongs ei̯, æi̯, oi̯, ɑi̯ (ŋei̯n 'child'), and before one (i̯ǽ.i̯o 'native banyan'); contrast syllabic i in i.bí.a 'lump'. Its non-syllabic status is clear only where it would be stressed if syllabic (p. 661). A predictable epenthetic i̯ stands before the glide j (p. 662). It contrasts with the glide j (ei̯u 'seven' : eju 'three') and with u̯ (p. 661); j is fricated and phonetically longer (pp. 654, 657).
